notes: Record checked: archived 2025-10-30, last commit 2024-08-28 ('StringRef::startswith was deprecated, use starts_with'), Apache-2.0, 2.4k stars, 188 forks; the README links the arXiv paper but gives no performance data. tier_reason: The gh-pages data.js holds paired opt and no-opt rows from the main-branch CI run at commit aad9b74 (2026-10-12), and every ML-KEM-768 cycle count in claimed_speedup matches exactly. The benchmark code is public (test/bench/bench_mlkem.c driven by ./scripts/tests bench --opt=opt|no_opt), flags are in test/mk/config.mk and .github/workflows/bench.yml, the compiler is the flake-locked nixpkgs nixos-26.05 GCC (nix/util.nix native-gcc), and the CPU is fixed by the EC2 instance type, so tier A stands.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC from the flake-locked nixpkgs nixos-26.05 (nix dev shell 'bench', toolchains_native = pkgs.gcc wrapped in nix/util.nix; exact version not printed in the opened files), on an Ubuntu 26.04 LTS AMI. Common flags from test/mk/config.mk: -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -std=c99 -pedantic. Per-target flags from .github/workflows/bench.yml: all EC2 rows add -flto and -DMLK_FORCE_AARCH64 or -DMLK_FORCE_X86_64; c7i: -mavx2 -mbmi2 -mpopcnt -march=sapphirerapids; c7a: -march=znver4; c6i: -march=icelake-server; c6a: -march=znver3; Graviton2: -mcpu=cortex-a76 -march=armv8.2-a; Graviton3: -march=armv8.4-a+sha3; Graviton4: -march=armv9-a+sha3; Graviton5: -march=armv9-a+sha3 -DMLK_SYS_AARCH64_FAST_SHA3. The opt and no-opt rows use identical flags; no-opt passes --opt=no_opt (OPT=0) to disable the native backends.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 247 stars, 69 forks; default ML-KEM in liboqs since 0.13.0 and in AWS-LC since v1.50.0, and so in rustls since 0.23.28 through its AWS-LC provider, per the README

notes: All 24 ML-KEM-768 values for c7i, c7a, Graviton2 and Graviton4 match data.js; across the 8 EC2 targets the C-backend-to-native ratios run from 1.90x (Graviton4 decaps) to 3.01x (c6a encaps), so '1.9x to 3.0x' holds. Shortcomings to record: the baseline is the project's own portable C backend (a C90 fork of pq-crystals ref), not the unmodified ref or another library; the numbers come from rolling CI history on mostly small shared EC2 VMs (only c7i is bare metal); the compiler version is pinned through flake.lock but not printed in the files read.
